## Context / Problem
Nothing prevents a future doc or script from re-teaching a removed verb, and nothing asserts that the hint registry's replacements are themselves live commands. Cites are on origin/main ca042ec0f49 (2026-10-20). The two code stories now clean every teaching surface themselves, so this story's proof that the scan bites uses the pre-store-move tree, not a docs-story revert.

## Approach
New `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_removed_cli_verbs_heldout.py` modelled on `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_bridge_vocabulary_stale_heldout.py:66-93`, parametrized over `_help_route._REMOVED_SPELLINGS`: (a) for every key, `route_for(key) is None`; `main([key])` exits 2 and stderr carries `invalid choice`, the key, and the exact hint line; the hint's word after `rebar ` is a live top-level route; when that route's parser has nested subcommands (`bridge`, `store`), the next word is one of its subparser choices, and for `rebar store <sub>` also a member of `_registry.STORE_ROUTES`. (b) A `git ls-files` scan of `docs/ templates/ examples/ src/rebar/ scripts/ .github/ AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md README.md` for `rebar <key>`, exempting only the Python statement `from rebar import` (key `import` preceded by `from `), not every `from rebar <key>`; a pattern test pins that "tickets from rebar export NDJSON" matches, excluding the frozen-history prefixes `docs/adr/ docs/archive/ docs/experiments/ reports/` and a whole-file allowlist (`CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/release-notes.md`, `docs/exit-codes.md`, `src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py`). The scan covers all of `src/rebar/`. On ca042ec0f49 it finds 2 lines: the `docs/user-guide.md:659` alias mention and the `rebar.import_tickets` docstring at `src/rebar/_lib_reads.py:110` ("from rebar export NDJSON"), which the store story's rewrite skipped through the same blanket `from ` lookbehind; `import_tickets` is not an MCP tool and the docstring is in no golden. (c) `src/rebar/_lib_reads.py:110` becomes "from ``rebar store export`` NDJSON", and `docs/user-guide.md:659` drops `rebar ` before the historical `bridge-status` spelling (the bridge-vocabulary guard already allows the bare name in that file), so the dict-driven scan needs no exclusion. Extend `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py` to assert no `help/<key>.txt` artifact survives for any key.

## Scope
`tests/interfaces/contracts/test_removed_cli_verbs_heldout.py` (new), `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py`, one line each in `docs/user-guide.md` and `src/rebar/_lib_reads.py`. Out of scope: all other source and docs.

## Testing
Red-then-green: in a throwaway worktree at the change's tree, restore `docs/user-guide.md` from c0cf1022671 (which still teaches `rebar fsck`, `rebar doctor`, `rebar compact-all`); the scan must fail naming that file, then pass on the merged tree. Both runs are recorded in the commit message. `make verify`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The test is parametrized over `_REMOVED_SPELLINGS` (25 keys) with no hard-coded copy of its keys.
- [x] Every hint's replacement resolves to a live route, its nested sub-verb (for `bridge` and `store`) is one of that parser's subcommand choices, and `store` subs are `STORE_ROUTES` members.
- [x] The scan is proven red-then-green: with `docs/user-guide.md` restored from c0cf1022671 it fails naming 10 lines of that file, with only the `_lib_reads.py` docstring reverted it fails naming line 110, and on the change's tree it passes (the commit message records the runs). It also asserts that README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/user-guide.md and src/rebar/_lib_reads.py were scanned, so a mis-scoped enumeration fails rather than passing vacuously.
- [x] No `help/<key>.txt` survives for any removed key (`test_no_help_artifact_survives_for_a_removed_spelling`).
- [x] The test runs in the `ubuntu-latest, py3.13` selection (`not integration and not external`) with no marker beyond `unit`.
- [x] `make verify` exits 0 with `PYPANDOC_PANDOC` set to pandoc 3.9 (19,827 passed on patch set 1; patch set 2 changed only that one test function, and its 3 contract files pass, 47 passed).
